column16: Club was PAE Kerkyra (AOK Kerkyra), the 2013 merger of AO Kerkyra (1968) with AO Kassiopi (1984); founded 1968 is the AO Kerkyra date. Older game records use Kerkira and AO Kerkyras for this club. Capacity: season page 3,000, stadium section of club page 2,685 all seated, no second source. colour1 Blue from 2016/17 home kit on club page; colour2 Red (inference) from the traditional AO Kerkyra red and navy kit. Division also agreed by RSSSF grk2017 (Kerkyra AO, 10th).

Name Ethnikos Piraeus - A.O. Mani from 2004, renamed Ethnikos Piraeus in 2007 per club page. First home match at Elliniko on 20 October 2007; ground before that date unknown. Capacity 2007/08 unknown: club site gives 5,450 for the former baseball stadium before extra stands (inference). Colours from nickname Blue-whites; main colour of that season's kit not confirmed. Division: no second source found (RSSSF 2007/08 page has no second level).

Capacity: club page and club site 9,000 after 2008/09 works, Hellinikon Stadium page says 10,000. Colours from nickname Blue-whites; main colour of that season's kit not confirmed. Division: no second source found (RSSSF 2008/09 page has no second level).

Reached the promotion play-offs. Capacity: club site 9,000 (archived January 2010), Hellinikon Stadium page 10,000. Colours from nickname Blue-whites; main colour not confirmed. Division: no second source found.

Second tier renamed Football League. Club placed 14th and demoted for forgery in the winter transfer window (RSSSF agrees). Stadium and capacity from club page and archived club site, not on RSSSF. Colours from nickname Blue-whites; main colour not confirmed.

First season in the second tier, promoted from Football League 2 South. RSSSF agrees name and division (11th). Stadium and capacity are from the current club page; 2011/12 capacity not confirmed, no second source. colour2 not found.

Promoted from Football League 2 North to fill places left by mergers and relegations. Played in the Northern Group, 12th, relegated (RSSSF agrees). Stadium and capacity: season page, citing a Greek league site; no second source. Club colours are white, green and red per club page; order of colour1 and colour2 (inference).

RSSSF name Aiolikos Mytilinis, Group A 11th, relegated after the play-out. Capacity: season page 3,000, club page 2,850, stadium page 3,300; no second source. Colours blue and white per Greek Wikipedia infobox; no second source. FotMob also lists Aiolikos Mitilini in this division.

Polish ę has no Windows-1252 form: written Drweca. From January 2005 to July 2006 the club played under the sponsor name KS Finishparkiet Nowe Miasto Lubawskie (both sources); RSSSF pol06 uses Drwęca Nowe Miasto Lubawskie. 18th, relegated. Capacity 2,000 (960 seated) per both sources, date of figure not given. Stadium name Stadion MOSiR from Polish Wikipedia; 90minut gives the address only.
